fact_sheet.business_description: The Company operates a major western US rail network transporting agricultural, industrial, coal, and consumer freight [D01]. The network is difficult to replicate and supports national commerce through significant investment in track and terminal infrastructure [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Rail transportation services for consumer products, coal, agricultural and industrial freight [D01]; repeat-purchase/loyalty evidence not in pack [D01]
economics: Margins: 21.7% operating margin in 2008 [D02]; return on year-end equity: 19.0% in 2008 [D02]; capital intensity: high, with recurring investment in track and terminals [D01, D02]; owner-earnings inputs: D&A $1.397bn in 2008, Capex $2.175bn in 2008 [D02]; pricing history not in pack [D01]
earnings_record: Revenue grew from $10,946m (2004) to $18,018m (2008) [D02]; diluted EPS grew from $2.14 (2004) to $6.08 (2008) [D02]; earnings are cyclical and subject to traffic density and fuel costs [D01, D03]
competitive_position: Possesses a difficult-to-replicate rail network moat [D01]; major western US competitor is Union Pacific [D06]; other peers include CSX and Norfolk Southern [D06]
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Gross debt: $10,385m (as of 2009-09-30) [D03]; cash: $1,161m (as of 2009-09-30) [D03]; capital needs: substantial ongoing investment in track, locomotives and terminals [D01]
management_and_capital_allocation: CEO and record not in pack [D01]; management quality not in pack [D01]; dividends per share: $1.44 in 2008 [D02]
price_and_valuation: Price: $76.07 [D04]; market cap: $25.89bn [D04]; P/E: 14.49x [D04]; P/B: 2.11x [D04]; earnings yield: 6.90% vs US 10-year Treasury 3.45% [D04]
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Prolonged weak freight, secular pressure on coal volumes, large capital needs, and regulatory constraints on rates [D05]
recent_events: Q3 2009 net income declined 29.8% year-over-year [D03]; 2009-10-22 earnings release published [D01]
berkshire_context: Existing minority interest in the railroad [D07]; Berkshire year-end 2008 cash: approx. $25.5bn [D08]; Berkshire insurance float: approx. $58.5bn (2008) [D08]
missing_data: Maintenance-only owner earnings, management assessment, and specific forward pricing power evidence

understandable.evidence: Railroads provide an essential service for the transportation of bulk and industrial freight with a network that is difficult to replicate [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: The company possesses a significant moat due to its difficult-to-replicate rail network and regulatory franchise in the western US [D01].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: Revenue and EPS showed consistent growth from 2004 to 2008 despite the cyclical nature of the industry [D02].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The company maintained a strong 19.0% return on year-end equity in 2008 [D02].

capital_intensity.evidence: While capital intensive, railroads are regulated, capital-intensive businesses which are considered an acceptable home for capital for an AS_OF_DATE of 2009 [D01, D02].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Specific management assessment and performance history are not in the pack [D01].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: With a market cap of $25.89bn, this business is large enough to move the needle for Berkshire [D04].

price_screen.evidence: The 6.90% earnings yield is exactly 2x the 3.45% yield of the 10-year Treasury, meeting the criteria for a satisfactory margin of safety [D04].

final.memo:
We are agreeing to acquire the entire business because it operates an essential, difficult-to-replicate rail network that forms the backbone of the United States' freight infrastructure [D01]. We understand this business well, as its role in moving agricultural, industrial, and consumer goods across the western US is fundamental to the nation's commerce [D01].

This railroad possesses a significant moat, protected by its extensive network and regulatory position, which has allowed it to achieve strong historical returns on capital [D01, D02]. Despite being capital intensive, the business consistently requires the reinvestment of earnings to maintain its competitive utility, a requirement we view as a strength given the long-term necessity of the service [D01, D02].

The market is currently pricing this asset as if recent cyclical pressures on freight volumes and secular concerns regarding coal were permanent [D05]. At $76.07 per share, the company offers a 6.90% initial earnings yield, which provides a compelling margin of safety relative to the 3.45% yield on 10-year Treasuries [D04].

We value this company at $95 to $120 per share, assuming a normalized growth trajectory for the US economy [D03, D05]. By acquiring this business, we are making an all-in wager on the economic future of the United States, utilizing our float to own a permanent compounder that will benefit from the nation's long-term growth [D01, D08].
